note: Course sample projects and advised work. Named students appear when they opt in. Studio samples are representative posted work from the courses — replace or rename as real teams allow.

projects.title: Grocery segments that change a promotion
projects.summary: Cluster a retail basket dataset, name the segments in language a category manager would use, and recommend one promotion change you would actually fund.

projects.title: Who churns, and who is just quiet
projects.summary: A classification project that separates true churn risk from dormancy, with a cost-sensitive evaluation and a one-page decision brief for a product owner.

projects.title: Redesigning a misleading public dashboard
projects.summary: Take a real dashboard that lies by accident, document the perceptual and statistical failures, and ship a redesign that a non-analyst can use under time pressure.

projects.title: One chart, one decision
projects.summary: A board-packet exercise: a single visual that forces a yes/no decision, with the discarded alternatives shown in an appendix.

projects.title: Reading the room on an earnings call
projects.summary: A multimodal project I designed into the new AI methods course: text, audio, and visual signals from an earnings call, with an explicit section on what the model must not be used for.

projects.title: A city's civic graph
projects.summary: Build a network from public social data, find communities, and write the management memo before you write the model card.

projects.title: Hiring scorecard for a twelve-person data team
projects.summary: From the micro-course I built: design a hiring and leveling scorecard that a non-technical manager can defend.

projects.title: First week with a messy operations extract
projects.summary: Explore, clean, and visualize a hostile CSV until the interesting question is obvious. Then make the chart that survives the handoff.

projects.title: How large is large enough?
projects.summary: A power and uncertainty brief for a product A/B test — the statistics course as a management deliverable.

projects.title: A model with a constraint you cannot ignore
projects.summary: Machine learning for business applications: fit the model, then put a real operating constraint next to the ROC curve and decide anyway.

projects.title: Inspection outcomes without leaking the future
projects.summary: Policy-facing machine learning: predict an inspection-related outcome with a leakage hunt as part of the grade.

projects.title: Three CSVs to a table a model can trust
projects.summary: Modern data management sample: design keys, clean joins, and document the warehouse table so next week's mining team does not invent the schema again.
